A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TAPIP3D. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original tracking experiments, architectural ablations, neighborhood-size sensitivity results, and inference-speed measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds blur, camera-pose perturbation, sparse-depth, and TAP-Vid-DAVIS evaluation results.

M1.justification: The 3D feature clouds, neighborhood-to-neighborhood attention, trajectory transformer, loss, and iterative inference procedure are retained. Window-length explanations, notation changes, and sparse-depth preprocessing do not establish a change to the proposed tracking model.

E1.justification: v3 adds TAP-Vid-DAVIS coverage and sparse-LiDAR input evaluation within the existing Waymo/TAPVid-3D domain, plus blurred-image and erroneous-camera-pose scenarios. Original coverage remains. The neighborhood-size paragraph now names Dynamic Replica correctly; v2 Table 7 already reported that dataset.

E2.justification: Corresponding original comparisons retain CoTracker3, SpatialTracker/SpaTracker, and DELTA as applicable. New appendix experiments reuse existing comparators. CUT3R is suggested as a possible alternative geometry estimator, without an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols apply Gaussian blur with strengths 0, 0.5, 1, and 2 and re-estimate depth; perturb camera orientations with Gaussian angular noise; and densify sparse LiDAR using nearest-neighbor interpolation on 50 Waymo sequences. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain. Expanded TAPVid metric descriptions clarify existing scoring rather than establish a metric change.

E4.justification: Appendices E.2–E.3 add controlled analyses of image-blur and camera-pose robustness, reported in Tables 8–9. Appendix C adds a pipeline runtime breakdown. Existing coordinate-system, N2N, neighborhood-selection, neighborhood-size, and stereo-example analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new Gaussian standard deviations specify input perturbations, not uncertainty estimates for reported performance.

E6.justification: v3 adds robustness results, sparse-depth scores, DAVIS AJ/APD/OA of 58.9/71.2/89.6, and component timings. Table 1 changes DELTA's average APD3D from 22.3 to 26.3; other original accuracy tables retain their values. SpaTracker's exact 14.6 FPS entry disappears, although the approximate speed comparison remains. New Table 9 reports DELTA AJ3D as 37.1, an unexplained mismatch with Table 2's 37.7.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the training loss, and the N2N complexity expression are unchanged in substance. Revised symbols distinguish video length, window length, and scale count; no new theoretical results, formal assumptions, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explicit 3D feature clouds, N2N attention, camera-stabilized tracking, and strong tracking performance when reliable depth is available. Added evaluations do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 expands the existing depth-quality limitation with temporal geometry consistency, depth flickering, incorrect surface connections, and failures involving distant or blurred elements. It explicitly discusses weaker monocular 2D performance and geometry estimation as a runtime bottleneck. These refine applicability boundaries while retaining the original interpretations of the method's benefits.

D1.justification: Appendix A explicitly lists inherited training augmentations; Appendices C and F add component timings and sparse-depth processing details. Existing hyperparameters and memory-saving details remain. v3 removes the promise to release code upon acceptance while retaining the project link; the PDFs do not establish whether actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to ODIN and Unifying 2D and 3D Vision-Language Understanding beside the feature representation, the Waymo Open Dataset for sparse-depth evaluation, and CUT3R in the efficiency discussion. The original related-work narrative and other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Local revisions clarify notation, sliding windows, and metrics. Limitations become a separate section, acknowledgements and conference identification are added, and appendix sections are reorganized, including moving speed analysis earlier. Most original prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Visual changes are localized: v3 adds appendix Tables 8–10 and replaces the original speed table with prose. Tables 3–4 and Figure 5 move with pagination. All five figures and the original substantive table designs are retained, with local formatting and spacing changes.

improvement.justification: The added robustness tests, sparse-depth and DAVIS evaluations, and explicit failure discussion make practical applicability easier to assess. Table 1 also corrects a baseline average. These gains outweigh the removed code-release promise and the new unexplained DELTA discrepancy between Tables 2 and 9. The core method and primary evidence were already established in v2, so the overall improvement is limited.
